indicators.note: round says the tramping word goes all the way around the word for about

parts.note: to pad is to tramp along on foot
re is Latin-derived crossword shorthand for about or concerning

explanation.surface: A vagrant wanders around and about, looking flayed by the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Peeled fruit has had its rind cut away, just as a skinned thing has lost its outer layer.

clue.text: Fops pay a call on birds

parts.note: to pop in is to pay a brief visit
jays are birds of the crow family

explanation.surface: Dandies go visiting some birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A vain, showy dandy was likened to a parrot, so the plural means conceited dandies.

definitions.note: Author's stands for author is, the definition

indicators.note: sound says the word for archaic advice is heard

parts.note: rede is an archaic word for advice

explanation.surface: A writer's tip: listen if the advice is old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, author of The Cloister and the Hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian novelist Charles Reade is a writer, so the name fits a writer clue.

indicators.note: sounds says the phrase for a fine hero is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a dandy is a fine fellow and a lion a hero, making dandy lion

explanation.surface: An ordinary watchmaker sounds like a splendid champion.
explanation.walkthrough: The common weed's seed head is called a clock, blown away to tell the time, so the plant 'makes' clocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A widespread yellow weed produces a fluffy seed head that children call a clock.

parts.note: to sup is to take supper, an old word for eating
porter is a dark beer once popular with London porters

explanation.surface: Advice on the order of a meal: food comes first, then the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' and the 'second' of the surface look like ordering instructions; 'first' is a link and 'second' is the definition, a duellist's second.
explanation.definitionFit: A second in a duel or boxing match backs up the principal, so is a backer.

parts.note: seamen are proverbially free-spending and carefree when ashore, spending like drunken mariners

explanation.definitionFit: Seamen ashore are proverbially reckless with money and carefree.

explanation.surface: Publicity people and old locomotives both blow their own trumpets.
explanation.definitionFit: Publicists puff (hype) products, and small steam locomotives or boats were nicknamed for their puffing.

clue.text: Stones of appeal to one's friends

parts.note: O is an exclamation of appeal, as in O Lord
pals are one's friends

explanation.surface: Gems that serve as an appeal to one's companions.
explanation.definitionFit: These gems are milky stones with a play of colour.

parts.note: tail-end Charlie is the last in line, and in cricket the weak batsmen come in late in the batting order

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the last few batsmen, who bat late, are the weakest; 'Charlie' recalls the RAF 'tail-end Charlie', the rear gunner.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-order batsman comes in to bat near the end of the innings.

clue.text: Put back the clock, tipped over

indicators.note: tipped over in a down clue turns the clock word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: a timer is a clock

explanation.surface: Someone resets a clock that has fallen over.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit is to send back or postpone, deferring a matter.

clue.text: Opener of case with a sort of fit-in flap

indicators.note: a sort of hints the letters of fit-in flap make some other form of word

explanation.surface: Instructions for making an envelope or case with a tuck-in flap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener of case' suggests a flap or catch, but it is the person who starts a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: The party who brings a legal action opens the court proceedings against the defendant.

clue.text: A "" Cross "" island-not Malta, it need hardly be said

parts.note: a cross is drawn as the letter X
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Not Malta, the famous George Cross island, but some other Cross island.
explanation.walkthrough: Malta was awarded the George Cross in 1942, so a 'Cross island' wants to be Malta; 'not Malta' points to a different island, the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-evident truth is a statement so obvious that it scarcely needs stating.

clue.text: One point in particular makes a girl cognate

indicators.note: in places the compass point within the word for particular

parts.note: a nice distinction is a particular, fussy one
E for east is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: A grammar note: one precise point makes a girl's name related to another word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cognate' is used in its old sense of a blood relation, not the linguistic one.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a female blood relative, a kinswoman.

explanation.surface: An exhausted spender finds the bank account overdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Over-spent means utterly exhausted (whacked), and having spent beyond one's means puts an account in deficit.

parts.note: A is a musical note
C stands for circa, about
to be quits is to be even, level with someone

explanation.surface: A banker's note about settling up evenly.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that clears a defendant releases them, setting them free of the charge.

explanation.surface: Someone fit for the post, though not without doubts.
explanation.definitionFit: Qualified means fit or entitled, and also limited by conditions, as in qualified praise.

clue.text: Old Bob fooled and slipped about

parts.note: a bob was an old British shilling, abbreviated s
kidded means fooled or teased

explanation.surface: An old man called Bob was tricked and skated around.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bob' was the shilling in pre-decimal British money, written s; 'Bob' looks like a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A car or foot sliding out of control on ice has slid sideways.

clue.text: Spain! I'm so moved — how it can rouse me !

indicators.note: moved suggests the letters of Spain, I'm and so are shifted around

explanation.surface: A lover of Spain exclaims how the country stirs their passions.
explanation.definitionFit: To impassion is to fill with passion, to stir up strong feelings.

indicators.note: the in of indeed puts the rearranged story inside the rest of the word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of story take an odd new order

explanation.surface: Exclamation of surprise at a weird tale of ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed' splits as 'in deed': STROY (an anagram of STORY, from 'strange') goes in DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wrecked beyond repair has been demolished.

indicators.note: sounds like says the word for bad marks is heard, not seen

parts.note: stains are bad marks on cloth

explanation.surface: A complaint about blemishes on a Surrey resident's record.
explanation.walkthrough: Staines is a town on the Thames in Surrey, so 'Surrey' stands for a place there.
explanation.definitionFit: The town lies in the English county, so the county name serves as an example-style pointer to it.

indicators.note: containing says the mug word holds the dry word

parts.note: a stein is a beer mug
TT is teetotal, meaning dry

explanation.surface: A tankard holding a dry Polish drink of port.
explanation.walkthrough: Stettin is the German name for Szczecin, a Baltic port in Poland; 'Polish' looks like a verb or wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Stettin, now Szczecin, is a harbour city on the Oder estuary in Poland.

parts.note: re means about or concerning
port is an old word for carriage or bearing

explanation.surface: A compass direction: knocking around, heading south.
explanation.definitionFit: The loud cracks of guns firing are their explosions, heard from afar.

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name
one who ate was not starving

explanation.surface: A well-fed, red-cheeked girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Roseate means rosy or pink, the flush of a healthy face.

parts.note: a lag is an old convict, and convicts do time, so this reads as convicts serving their sentences

explanation.definitionFit: Inmates of a jail are convicts serving time.

indicators.note: In puts the passionate word inside the river

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
hot means very passionate

explanation.surface: A steamy scene from a film called The River.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a picture taken with a camera.

clue.text: Once a tricky thing for travellers to cross

indicators.note: tricky hints the letters of once and a are worked into a cunning rearrangement

explanation.surface: A treacherous obstacle that travellers once faced.
explanation.definitionFit: A vast sea separates continents, and voyagers have to traverse it.

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims approval at something unadulterated.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer can mean utter or unmixed, and sheer fabric is very fine and diaphanous.

clue.text: They have rows — a number, in fact

explanation.surface: People forever arguing, and there are lots of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' reads as quarrels but means rowing: a rowing crew of eight oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing crew of oarsmen is named for its size, and the word is also a number after seven.

parts.note: O is the round figure nought, nothing
to pine is to long for something

explanation.surface: Grasping nothing for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold a view is to think or state it as an opinion.

clue.text: Drink one at a time with playful provocation

parts.note: tea is a drink
singly means one at a time

explanation.surface: Taking a sip at a time while gently mocking someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Taunting playfully is to tease, so the adverb describes doing something in a mocking, playful way.

clue.text: Canon, with dire trouble, gets decree

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters of canon and dire are stirred up into disorder

explanation.surface: A church canon, in dire straits, receives an official order.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative order or regulation, a formal decree.

clue.text: Not a friendly name for a man put down

parts.note: taken as written
Ed is a friendly short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Insulting a man by using an unfriendly name for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Something written down for record has been recorded in a notebook.
